code: library(sf) library(spatialkit)  set.seed(11) n  <- 350 xy <- data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000)) D  <- as.matrix(dist(xy)) field <- as.numeric(t(chol(exp(-D / 70) + diag(1e-8, n))) %*% rnorm(n)) xy$a  <- rnorm(n) xy$b  <- rnorm(n) xy$z  <- 1.5 * xy$a + field + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3) pts   <- st_as_sf(xy, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632) lm_fit <- function(train_sf, response_var = "z", predictor_vars = c("a", "b")) {   d   <- st_drop_geometry(train_sf)   # With no predictors the model is intercept-only: "z ~ 1", not "z ~ ".   rhs <- if (length(predictor_vars)) paste(predictor_vars, collapse = " + ") else "1"   fml <- as.formula(paste(response_var, "~", rhs))   new_spatial_fit(     subclass       = "lmsurf_fit",     engine         = lm(fml, data = d),     formula        = fml,     response_var   = response_var,     predictor_vars = predictor_vars,     data_sf        = train_sf   ) } predict.lmsurf_fit <- function(object, newdata = NULL, ...) {   if (is.null(newdata)) return(fitted(object$engine))   as.numeric(predict(object$engine, newdata = st_drop_geometry(newdata))) } residuals.lmsurf_fit <- function(object, ...) residuals(object$engine) fitted.lmsurf_fit    <- function(object, ...) fitted(object$engine) for (g in c("predict", "residuals", "fitted"))   registerS3method(g, "lmsurf_fit", get(paste0(g, ".lmsurf_fit")))  fit <- lm_fit(pts)

code: grid <- create_grid_polygons(hull, target_cells = 200, type = "square") gp   <- suppressWarnings(st_centroid(grid)) set.seed(2) gp$a <- rnorm(nrow(gp)) gp$b <- rnorm(nrow(gp), mean = 3)     # shifted well outside the training range  aoa <- area_of_applicability(gp, model = fit) aoa ## Area of applicability (Meyer & Pebesma 2021) ##  ##   predictors  : 2 (a, b) ##   weighted    : no (all predictors count equally: the model carries no variable importance) ##   training    : 350 points ##   reference   : nearest other training point (no folds supplied) ##   normaliser  : 1.7610 (mean pairwise distance) ##   threshold   : 0.1552 (outlier-removed max of training DI) ##   location    : not measured ##  ##   64 of 225 prediction points inside the AOA (28.4%) ##  ## Predictions outside the AOA are extrapolations; the cross-validated ## performance estimate does not cover them. plot(aoa) inside <- !is.na(aoa$aoa$AOA) & aoa$aoa$AOA c(inside = sum(inside), outside_or_unknown = sum(!inside)) ##             inside outside_or_unknown  ##                 64                161

code: # 5. Build folds that hold out whole regions.  block_size is a distance in #    the CRS's units, here metres. Fit and score.  cv_rf() fits a random forest inside every fold and pools #    the held-out predictions; the same call with random folds is the number #    a random split would have reported. cv_random  <- cv_rf(obs, "rate", "nw_share", folds = random,  num_trees = 300, seed = 1) cv_blocked <- cv_rf(obs, "rate", "nw_share", folds = blocked, num_trees = 300, seed = 1) rbind(random = cv_random$overall[, c("RMSE", "MAE", "R2")],       blocked = cv_blocked$overall[, c("RMSE", "MAE", "R2")]) ##             RMSE      MAE          R2 ## random  1.604483 1.120585 -0.04952951 ## blocked 1.365868 1.056827  0.29493961 # The pooled number hides how much the folds disagree; with a hundred # observations they disagree a lot. rbind(random  = range(cv_random$fold_metrics$RMSE),       blocked = range(cv_blocked$fold_metrics$RMSE)) ##              [,1]     [,2] ## random  1.0390731 2.189466 ## blocked 0.9565161 1.935064

code: # 7. Predict on a grid over the study area and ask where the prediction is #    extrapolating.  The area of applicability compares each grid cell's #    predictors with the training data, using the folds above as the #    reference, so the threshold is the one the cross-validated score was #    earned under. fit  <- fit_rf_model(obs, "rate", "nw_share", num_trees = 300, seed = 1) surf <- predict_surface(fit, n_cells = 4000, covariates = obs,                         boundary = boundary) aoa  <- area_of_applicability(surf, model = fit, folds = blocked) aoa ## Area of applicability (Meyer & Pebesma 2021) ##  ##   predictors  : 1 (nw_share) ##   weighted    : no (all predictors count equally: the model has no out-of-bag skill (OOB R-squared -0.059), so its importances are noise) ##   training    : 100 points ##   reference   : nearest point outside each of 4 CV folds (block_kfold) ##   normaliser  : 1.1527 (mean pairwise distance) ##   threshold   : 0.0440 (outlier-removed max of training DI) ##   location    : not measured ##  ##   2454 of 2454 prediction points inside the AOA (100.0%) library(ggplot2) # predict_surface() returns the grid as points (cell centres), so the surface # is drawn as coloured points; the county points sit on top in black. ggplot() +   geom_sf(data = surf, aes(colour = .pred), size = 1.1) +   geom_sf(data = boundary, fill = NA, colour = "grey20") +   geom_sf(data = obs, size = 0.5, colour = "black") +   scale_colour_viridis_c(name = "predicted rate") +   theme_void() +   ggtitle("Predicted SIDS rate per thousand births")

code: set.seed(42) xy    <- st_coordinates(centres) D     <- as.matrix(dist(xy)) field <- as.numeric(t(chol(exp(-D / 120e3) + diag(1e-8, nrow(D)))) %*%                       rnorm(nrow(D)))  pts <- centres pts$elev <- rnorm(nrow(pts)) pts$z    <- 0.8 * pts$elev + 2 * field + rnorm(nrow(pts), sd = 0.3) # A learner with no optional dependencies: a linear trend surface in the # coordinates, plus the one covariate. trend_fit <- function(train_sf, ...) {   d  <- st_drop_geometry(train_sf)   co <- st_coordinates(train_sf)   d$x <- co[, 1]; d$y <- co[, 2]   new_spatial_fit(subclass = "trend_fit",                   engine = stats::lm(z ~ elev + x + y, data = d),                   formula = z ~ elev + x + y, response_var = "z",                   predictor_vars = "elev", data_sf = train_sf) } predict.trend_fit <- function(object, newdata = NULL, ...) {   if (is.null(newdata)) return(stats::fitted(object$engine))   d  <- st_drop_geometry(newdata)   co <- st_coordinates(newdata)   d$x <- co[, 1]; d$y <- co[, 2]   as.numeric(stats::predict(object$engine, newdata = d)) } residuals.trend_fit <- function(object, ...) stats::residuals(object$engine) fitted.trend_fit    <- function(object, ...) stats::fitted(object$engine) for (.g in c("predict", "residuals", "fitted"))   registerS3method(.g, "trend_fit", get(paste0(.g, ".trend_fit")))  folds <- make_folds(pts, k = 5, method = "block_kfold", block_size = 100e3,                     seed = 1) cv    <- cv_spatial(pts, "z", "elev", trend_fit, folds = folds) fit   <- trend_fit(pts)

code: library(sf) library(spatialkit)  knn_fit <- function(train_sf, response_var = "z", k = 5L) {   new_spatial_fit(     subclass       = "knnsurf_fit",     engine         = list(xy = st_coordinates(train_sf),                           y = st_drop_geometry(train_sf)[[response_var]],                           k = k),     formula        = as.formula(paste(response_var, "~ 1")),     response_var   = response_var,     predictor_vars = character(0),     data_sf        = train_sf   ) }  predict.knnsurf_fit <- function(object, newdata = NULL, ...) {   e  <- object$engine   xy <- if (is.null(newdata)) e$xy else st_coordinates(newdata)   vapply(seq_len(nrow(xy)), function(i) {     d <- sqrt((e$xy[, 1] - xy[i, 1])^2 + (e$xy[, 2] - xy[i, 2])^2)     mean(e$y[order(d)[seq_len(min(e$k, length(d)))]])   }, numeric(1)) } residuals.knnsurf_fit <- function(object, ...) object$engine$y - predict(object) fitted.knnsurf_fit    <- function(object, ...) predict(object)  registerS3method("predict",   "knnsurf_fit", predict.knnsurf_fit) registerS3method("residuals", "knnsurf_fit", residuals.knnsurf_fit) registerS3method("fitted",    "knnsurf_fit", fitted.knnsurf_fit)  knn_fn <- function(train_sf, ...) knn_fit(train_sf, "z", k = 5L) set.seed(7) n  <- 400 xy <- data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000)) D  <- as.matrix(dist(xy)) xy$z <- as.numeric(t(chol(exp(-D / 60) + diag(1e-8, n))) %*% rnorm(n)) +         rnorm(n, sd = 0.3) pts  <- st_as_sf(xy, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632)

code: n_points <- 300  pts_raw    <- st_sample(nc_boundary, size = n_points, type = "random") pts_coords <- st_coordinates(pts_raw) x_coords   <- pts_coords[, 1] y_coords   <- pts_coords[, 2]  elevation <- scale(x_coords)[, 1] * 500 + rnorm(n_points, 3000, 400)  city1 <- c(1530000, 550000)   # Charlotte-ish in EPSG:2264 city2 <- c(2150000, 750000)   # Raleigh-ish dist_to_city <- pmin(   sqrt((x_coords - city1[1])^2 + (y_coords - city1[2])^2),   sqrt((x_coords - city2[1])^2 + (y_coords - city2[2])^2) ) pop_density <- pmax(exp(-dist_to_city / 400000) * 5000 + rnorm(n_points, 200, 100), 10)  spatial_field <- 20 * sin(x_coords / 250000) * cos(y_coords / 250000)  y_response <- 50 +   0.01  * elevation +   0.005 * pop_density +   spatial_field +   rnorm(n_points, 0, 5)  points_sf <- st_sf(   y           = y_response,   elevation   = elevation,   pop_density = pop_density,   geometry    = pts_raw ) ggplot() +   geom_sf(data = nc_boundary, fill = "grey95", colour = "black") +   geom_sf(data = points_sf, aes(colour = y), size = 1.1) +   scale_colour_viridis_c(name = "Response (y)") +   theme_void() +   ggtitle("Raw observation points, North Carolina")

code: #' Assign points to cells, summarise, and draw a choropleth. make_choropleth <- function(tess, boundary, points, title = NULL) {   cells    <- tess$cells   assigned <- assign_features_to_polygons(points, cells, polygon_id_col = "cell_id")    stats_df <- summarize_by_cell(assigned, response_var = "y",                                 id_col = "cell_id")   cells    <- left_join(cells, as.data.frame(stats_df)[, c("cell_id", "resp_mean_y")],                         by = "cell_id")    plot_tessellation_map(     tessellation_sf = cells,     boundary        = boundary,     fill_col        = "resp_mean_y",     palette         = "viridis",     tile_alpha      = 0.9,     outline_col     = "white",     outline_size    = 0.3,     boundary_col    = "grey20",     boundary_size   = 0.8,     legend_title    = "Mean y",     title           = title,     subtitle        = sprintf("%d cells | %d observations",                               nrow(cells), nrow(points))   ) } make_choropleth(tess_voronoi, nc_boundary, points_sf, "Voronoi tessellation") make_choropleth(tess_hex, nc_boundary, points_sf, "Hexagonal grid") make_choropleth(tess_square, nc_boundary, points_sf, "Square grid") make_choropleth(tess_tri, nc_boundary, points_sf, "Delaunay triangulation") library(patchwork)  # The cell means of all three, so the colour scale can span them. cell_means <- function(tess) {   a <- assign_features_to_polygons(points_sf, tess$cells, polygon_id_col = "cell_id")   summarize_by_cell(a, response_var = "y", id_col = "cell_id")$resp_mean_y } lims <- range(unlist(lapply(list(tess_voronoi, tess_hex, tess_square), cell_means)),               na.rm = TRUE)  # One line per map instead of a title and a subtitle, and the cell count taken # from the tessellation rather than typed in. bare <- function(tess, label) {   make_choropleth(tess, nc_boundary, points_sf) +     ggplot2::scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Mean y", limits = lims) +     ggplot2::labs(title = sprintf("%s, %d cells", label, nrow(tess$cells)),                   subtitle = NULL) +     ggplot2::theme(plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = ggplot2::rel(1))) }  (bare(tess_voronoi, "Voronoi") /  bare(tess_hex,     "Hex") /  bare(tess_square,  "Square")) +   plot_layout(guides = "collect") +   plot_annotation(title = "Tessellation comparison, cell-level mean response")

code: library(sf) library(spatialkit)  set.seed(42) n  <- 400 xy <- data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000)) D  <- as.matrix(dist(xy)) xy$w <- rnorm(n) # Mostly a smooth spatial field, with a weak measured predictor on top. xy$z <- 0.5 * xy$w +   as.numeric(t(chol(exp(-D / 80) + diag(1e-8, n))) %*% rnorm(n)) +   rnorm(n, sd = 0.3) site <- st_as_sf(xy, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632) tess  <- build_tessellation(site, boundary = clip_target_for(site, quiet = TRUE),                             method = "hex", approx_n_cells = 24, quiet = TRUE) asg   <- assign_features_to_polygons(site, tess$cells) cells <- summarize_by_cell(asg, "z", cells_sf = tess$cells, deff = "kish")  populated <- st_drop_geometry(cells)[cells$n > 1 & !is.na(cells$n), ] head(populated[, c("poly_id", "n", "resp_mean_z", "..se_resp_z",                    "..pooled_resp_z")], 4) #>   poly_id  n resp_mean_z ..se_resp_z ..pooled_resp_z #> 2       2 12  -0.3553720   0.3840250     -0.32153305 #> 3       3  6  -0.7977035   0.6491918     -0.54245922 #> 4       4  2  -1.8546732   0.1801251     -0.82499383 #> 5       5 14   0.0554452   0.7258217      0.04565301 trend_fit <- function(train_sf, ...) {   d <- st_drop_geometry(train_sf)   d$x <- st_coordinates(train_sf)[, 1]   d$y <- st_coordinates(train_sf)[, 2]   new_spatial_fit("trend_fit", engine = lm(z ~ w + poly(x, 3) * poly(y, 3), data = d),                   formula = z ~ w + poly(x, 3) * poly(y, 3), response_var = "z",                   predictor_vars = "w", data_sf = train_sf) } predict.trend_fit <- function(object, newdata = NULL, ...) {   if (is.null(newdata)) return(fitted(object$engine))   d <- st_drop_geometry(newdata)   d$x <- st_coordinates(newdata)[, 1]   d$y <- st_coordinates(newdata)[, 2]   as.numeric(predict(object$engine, newdata = d)) } residuals.trend_fit <- function(object, ...) residuals(object$engine) fitted.trend_fit    <- function(object, ...) fitted(object$engine) for (g in c("predict", "residuals", "fitted"))   registerS3method(g, "trend_fit", get(paste0(g, ".trend_fit"))) # The blocks are sized to the field's own correlation: its effective range is # 3 x 80 = 240 units, so 250-unit blocks hold out whole patches.  On real data # the range is estimated, by estimate_sac_range() or make_folds(auto_range = # TRUE); vignette("spatial-cross-validation") is about that choice. random  <- cv_spatial(site, "z", "w", fit_fn = trend_fit,                       folds = make_folds(site, k = 5, method = "random_kfold", seed = 1)) blocked <- cv_spatial(site, "z", "w", fit_fn = trend_fit,                       folds = make_folds(site, k = 5, method = "block_kfold",                                          block_size = 250, seed = 1))  c(random  = random$overall$RMSE,   blocked = blocked$overall$RMSE,   ratio   = blocked$overall$RMSE / random$overall$RMSE) #>   random  blocked    ratio  #> 1.011489 1.584805 1.566804 residual_morans_i(trend_fit(site)) #> Residual Moran's I = 0.3314   (E[I] = -0.0025, sd = 0.0236) #>   z = 14.136, p = 2.275e-45 #>   null: randomisation moments, approximate for these residuals; n = 400, df = 399 #>   residual kurtosis 3.502 (3 = Gaussian) #>   weights: 400 x 400 dgCMatrix, 8 neighbour(s) per row; not retained, keep_weights = TRUE to keep it

code: library(sf) #> Linking to GEOS 3.12.1, GDAL 3.8.4, PROJ 9.4.0; sf_use_s2() is TRUE set.seed(1) n <- 120 train <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000),              a = rnorm(n), b = rnorm(n)),   coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632 ) train$z <- 2 * train$a - train$b + rnorm(n, 0, 0.3)  # Prediction points, some of them well outside the training predictor range newpts <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(50, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(50, 0, 1000),              a = c(rnorm(40), rnorm(10, 8)), b = rnorm(50)),   coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632 )  res <- area_of_applicability(newpts, train_sf = train,                              predictor_vars = c("a", "b")) res #> Area of applicability (Meyer & Pebesma 2021) #>  #>   predictors  : 2 (a, b) #>   weighted    : no (all predictors count equally: no model was given) #>   training    : 120 points #>   reference   : nearest other training point (no folds supplied) #>   normaliser  : 1.7777 (mean pairwise distance) #>   threshold   : 0.2899 (outlier-removed max of training DI) #>   location    : not measured #>  #>   39 of 50 prediction points inside the AOA (78.0%) #>  #> Predictions outside the AOA are extrapolations; the cross-validated #> performance estimate does not cover them. table(res$aoa$AOA) #>  #> FALSE  TRUE  #>    11    39

code: library(sf) set.seed(1) n <- 400 east  <- runif(n, 0, 1e4) north <- runif(n, 0, 1e4) all_pts <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(x = 5e5 + east, y = 5e6 + north,              income = 30 + 5 * sin(east / 2000) + 5 * cos(north / 1500) +                rnorm(n)),   coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632 ) pts    <- all_pts[1:350, ] newpts <- all_pts[351:400, ]  # The count from a size, the cells, the observations in them, the values, # all at the defaults: pooled values at 4.5 observations per cell. prof  <- resolution_profile(pts, "income") sel   <- select_resolution(prof) seeds <- get_voronoi_seeds(method = "kmeans", n = sel, sample_points = pts) tess  <- build_tessellation(seeds, method = "voronoi") #> create_voronoi_polygons(): deriving boundary from the cover the seeds carry (its hull or polygons, grown by 2% of the diagonal). asg   <- assign_features_to_polygons(pts, tess$cells, polygon_id_col = "cell_id") out   <- summarize_by_cell(asg, "income", id_col = "cell_id",                            cells_sf = tess$cells, obs_level = 0.90)  # The value at other locations, each placed in the cell of its nearest # seed.  `tess$index` gives the cell of each seed. seeds$cell_id <- tess$index at <- cell_values_at(newpts, out, asg, "income", id_col = "cell_id",                      seeds = seeds) head(at) #>   cell_id    value estimate   obs_lo   obs_hi filled filled_from dist_nearest #> 1      41 28.48055   pooled 26.02536 31.09205  FALSE          NA     238.4435 #> 2       5 37.30667   pooled 34.85149 39.91818  FALSE          NA     115.6546 #> 3      64 22.93542   pooled 20.48023 25.54692  FALSE          NA     271.2353 #> 4      28 38.91665   pooled 36.46147 41.52815  FALSE          NA     367.1291 #> 5      75 20.96892   pooled 18.51374 23.58042  FALSE          NA     227.2415 #> 6      10 34.21084   pooled 31.75566 36.82234  FALSE          NA     351.8853 #>   dist_ratio #> 1  0.9403784 #> 2  0.4561211 #> 3  1.0697034 #> 4  1.4478917 #> 5  0.8961997 #> 6  1.3877727 attr(at, "values_at") #> Cell values at other locations: income, the pooled value #>   cell        : of the nearest seed (the Voronoi cell before its clip to the cover) #>   interval    : 90% for ONE OBSERVATION (obs_lo, obs_hi), centred on the value #>   scored rows : 350 rows at 350 locations, measured in EPSG:32632 #>   spacing     : 253.6, the median distance from a scored location to the #>                 nearest other; dist_ratio is dist_nearest over it #>   filled      : no location #>   count       : 78 cells, set by size (the summary's record, in `count_rule`) #> Away from the observations no interval here is calibrated.  # Without the seeds a location is placed in the polygon that holds it.  One # beyond the layer's edge lies in no polygon: it is filled from the cell of # the nearest observation, and `dist_ratio` says how far that is. beyond <- st_sf(geometry = st_sfc(st_point(c(5e5 + 2e4, 5e6 + 5e3)), crs = 32632)) cell_values_at(rbind(st_sf(geometry = st_geometry(newpts[1:2, ])), beyond),                out, asg, "income", id_col = "cell_id") #>   cell_id    value estimate   obs_lo   obs_hi filled filled_from dist_nearest #> 1      41 28.48055   pooled 26.02536 31.09205  FALSE          NA     238.4435 #> 2       5 37.30667   pooled 34.85149 39.91818  FALSE          NA     115.6546 #> 3      NA 25.14089   pooled 22.68570 27.75239   TRUE          78   10204.7354 #>   dist_ratio #> 1  0.9403784 #> 2  0.4561211 #> 3 40.2456524

code: if (requireNamespace("ranger", quietly = TRUE)) {   library(sf)   set.seed(1)   pts <- st_as_sf(     data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(60, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(60, 0, 1000),                a = rnorm(60), b = rnorm(60)),     coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632   )   # An offset keeps the response away from zero, where MAPE is undefined.   pts$z <- 10 + 2 * pts$a - pts$b + rnorm(60, 0, 0.3)   # Two predictor sets for the same learner: the model that leaves `b` out   # against the one that has it.  These are in-sample (out-of-bag) numbers;   # compare_models_cv() scores the same question on spatial folds.   fits <- list(a_only = fit_rf_model(pts, "z", "a", num_trees = 100, seed = 1),                a_and_b = fit_rf_model(pts, "z", c("a", "b"), num_trees = 100, seed = 1))   compare_models(fits) } #>     model  n      RMSE       MAE      MAPE    SMAPE        R2 Adj_R2 n_MAPE #> 1  a_only 60 1.2209445 0.9721158 10.181689 9.914608 0.6804065     NA     60 #> 2 a_and_b 60 0.7698265 0.5989365  6.332639 6.133211 0.8729450     NA     60 #>   n_SMAPE metric_basis AICc LOOIC bandwidth_is_fallback convergence_ok #> 1      60   out-of-bag   NA    NA                    NA             NA #> 2      60   out-of-bag   NA    NA                    NA             NA #>   gp_adequacy resid_morans_I resid_morans_z resid_morans_p resid_morans_null #> 1        <NA>    -0.04684408     -0.5291138      0.5967265     randomisation #> 2        <NA>    -0.06447357     -0.8456951      0.3977229     randomisation #>   resid_morans_basis #> 1         out-of-bag #> 2         out-of-bag

title: Model-agnostic spatial cross-validation — cv_spatial
code: library(sf) set.seed(1) n <- 80 site <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000),              elev = rnorm(n)),   coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632 ) site$price <- 10 + 0.01 * (st_coordinates(site)[, 1] - 5e5) +   2 * site$elev + rnorm(n)  # 1. A fit_fn returning a spatial_fit of your own subclass. lm_fit <- function(train_sf) {   new_spatial_fit(     subclass       = "lm_fit",     engine         = lm(price ~ elev, st_drop_geometry(train_sf)),     formula        = price ~ elev,     response_var   = "price",     predictor_vars = "elev",     data_sf        = train_sf   ) }  # 2. The predict() method cv_spatial() scores each fold with. Without it #    every fold fails and `overall` comes back all-NA. predict.lm_fit <- function(object, newdata = NULL, ...) {   if (is.null(newdata)) newdata <- object$data_sf   as.numeric(stats::predict(object$engine, st_drop_geometry(newdata))) } registerS3method("predict", "lm_fit", predict.lm_fit)  cv <- cv_spatial(site, "price", "elev", fit_fn = lm_fit, k = 3, seed = 1) #> cv_spatial(): no folds supplied -- using spatial block k-fold CV (k=3). cv$overall #>       RMSE      MAE     MAPE    SMAPE        R2 Adj_R2 n_pred n_MAPE n_SMAPE #> 1 3.472328 3.009688 21.29953 20.27029 0.2341257     NA     80     80      80 # Compare these before trusting the metrics above; fold_status says why # any fold is missing from fold_metrics. c(attempted = cv$n_folds_attempted, succeeded = cv$n_folds_succeeded) #> attempted succeeded  #>         3         3  cv$fold_status #>   fold status message #> 1    1     ok         #> 2    2     ok         #> 3    3     ok          # 3. A metric of your own beside the built-in ones: per fold and pooled. med_ae <- function(y, yhat) c(MedAE = stats::median(abs(y - yhat))) cv2 <- cv_spatial(site, "price", "elev", fit_fn = lm_fit, k = 3, seed = 1,                   metrics = med_ae) #> cv_spatial(): no folds supplied -- using spatial block k-fold CV (k=3). cv2$overall$MedAE #> [1] 2.981173 cv2$fold_metrics[, c("fold", "RMSE", "MedAE")] #>   fold     RMSE    MedAE #> 1    1 3.793601 3.536960 #> 2    2 3.198481 2.590833 #> 3    3 3.359840 2.678648

code: if (requireNamespace("gstat", quietly = TRUE)) {   library(sf)   # A Gaussian random field with an exponential covariance: range   # parameter 100, so the true effective range is 3 x 100 = 300, plus a   # small nugget.   set.seed(9)   n <- 150   xy <- data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000))   D  <- as.matrix(dist(xy))   xy$z <- as.numeric(t(chol(exp(-D / 100) + diag(0.1, n))) %*% rnorm(n))   pts <- st_as_sf(xy, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632)   r <- estimate_sac_range(pts, response_var = "z")   # print() throughout, because only the last value of a braced block is   # shown on its own, and every one of these is worth reading.   print(r)                              # the effective range, in metres   print(attr(r, "directional"))         # the four directional ranges   print(attr(r, "variogram_model"))     # the fitted model behind it   print(attr(r, "structure_p"))         # the test for spatial structure    # A field whose range the data cannot pin down: the variogram never   # reaches a sill within the lags fitted, so the answer is NA with the   # refused value attached rather than a long range asserted.   xy$trend <- sin(xy$x / 400) + rnorm(n, sd = 0.2)   r2 <- estimate_sac_range(st_as_sf(xy, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632),                            response_var = "trend")   print(r2)   attr(r2, "rejected_reason")   attr(r2, "rejected_range")    # White noise: no structure, so no range.   xy$noise <- rnorm(n)   r3 <- estimate_sac_range(st_as_sf(xy, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632),                            response_var = "noise")   attr(r3, "rejected_reason") } #> 292.1814  #>   directional: 0 deg = 248.1608, 45 deg = 413.7318, 90 deg = 617.9676, 135 deg = 426.5880  (ratio 2.49) #>   in metres of EPSG:32632; code: The residual test rests on fits of points on a 100 km square whose floor is 32 to 33 km.  Sampled fits: ten of a response with a component below the floor (a field with an 8 or 12 km range, alone or beside a plane or a field with a 90 km range) had p of 5.3e-10 to 0.014, and five of the ten had a posterior that reads \code{"ok"}; twelve of a response with none (planes, bowls, a sine, fields with ranges of 45 to 200 km) had p of 0.66 to 0.97.  At the posterior mode of the same model, computed without sampling, the test was significant in 0 of 160 fits of fields with ranges of 45 to 200 km and in 3 of 120 fits of a plane, a bowl and a sine (one noise draw of the 40, shared by the three, whose own Moran's I has p = 0.003); and in 16 to 18 of 20 fits of each of four responses with an 8 km field in them, where the length-scale at the mode was below the floor in 0 or 1 of the 20.  On a fit with nothing left over the test is conservative, because the surface takes up part of the noise and leaves the residuals slightly negatively autocorrelated (median I of -0.03 to -0.07).  It is not sharp just below the floor: a field with a 20 km range was significant in 8 of 20 fits, and there it is the length-scale draws that report it (\code{"below_resolution"}).  An exponential field has structure at every scale and can be reported with a range above the floor (8 of 20 fits at 60 km).  The 5 percent level is the usual one and is not tuned; with many rows a small leftover autocorrelation is significant, so read the size of I beside its p.  "No variance that can be told from zero" is decided on the Gaussian process's share of the variance, \code{sdgp^2 / (sdgp^2 + sigma^2)}: its 2.5 percent quantile is under 0.01.  On nine fits that quantile was 0.000 to 0.003 for the three with nothing for the process to find and 0.17 to 0.94 for the six with a surface; the threshold rests on those nine.  It does not mark off a response whose structure is all below the floor: on five fits of a field with an 8 km range under a 33 km floor the quantile was 0.000, 0.000, 0.001, 0.015 and 0.019, so two of the five count as carrying a share, and it is the residual test that reports them.  The share exists for a gaussian or lognormal family.  For any other family the length-scales decide instead: the process is not identified when on every axis the posterior kept more than three quarters of its prior's variance and the largest gap between its distribution function and the prior's is under 0.30.  That second rule has been checked on the length-scale draws of the same nine gaussian fits, where it agrees with the share on eight, and on no fit of another family. \code{$info$gp_adequacy$identified_by} says which rule was used.  The width of the length-scale posterior does not decide by itself, because a posterior that moved to longer length-scales is wider than its prior; and the share of draws below the floor cannot detect an unidentified process, because a posterior the data did not move puts 1 percent below the floor, the same as the prior.

title: How far the held-out points sit from the training data — fold_separation
code: library(sf) set.seed(1) n <- 200 pts <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000)),   coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632 )  # Random folds put a training point close to every held-out one. random  <- make_folds(pts, k = 4, method = "random_kfold", seed = 1) print(fold_separation(random, pts, sac = 200)) #> Fold separation: random_kfold, 4 fold(s), 200 held-out point(s) (EPSG:32632) #>   autocorrelation range: 200 (in metres, like the distances) #>  #>  fold n_train n_test min_dist median_dist mean_cor #>     1     150     50    4.696       36.95     0.57 #>     2     150     50    3.835       42.14     0.55 #>     3     150     50    3.835       38.52     0.58 #>     4     150     50    4.696       45.79     0.53 #>  #>   Held-out points sit a median of 41.61 from their nearest training #>   point; the closest is 3.835 away. Under the range of 200 that leaves a #>   mean correlation of 0.56 between a held-out point and its nearest #>   training point (exp(-3 d / range) averaged over the hold-out: 1 at #>   distance 0, 0.05 at the range). #>   No prediction target is given, so these are distances and no conclusion #>   about the score: a cross-validated error reads low when the hold-out #>   sits closer to its training data than the locations to be predicted do, #>   and high when it sits farther. Pass `prediction_points` to compare the #>   two.  # Blocked folds hold out whole neighbourhoods, so the distances grow. blocked <- make_folds(pts, k = 4, method = "block_kfold",                       block_size = 250, seed = 1) print(fold_separation(blocked, pts, sac = 200)) #> Fold separation: block_kfold, 4 fold(s), 200 held-out point(s) (EPSG:32632) #>   autocorrelation range: 200 (in metres, like the distances) #>  #>  fold n_train n_test n_blocks min_dist median_dist mean_cor #>     1     152     48        2    23.02       111.9     0.23 #>     2     143     57        3    29.04       169.5     0.14 #>     3     152     48        2    21.03       118.3     0.22 #>     4     153     47        2    21.03       115.9     0.23 #>  #>   Held-out points sit a median of 123.5 from their nearest training #>   point; the closest is 21.03 away. Under the range of 200 that leaves a #>   mean correlation of 0.20 between a held-out point and its nearest #>   training point (exp(-3 d / range) averaged over the hold-out: 1 at #>   distance 0, 0.05 at the range). #>   No prediction target is given, so these are distances and no conclusion #>   about the score: a cross-validated error reads low when the hold-out #>   sits closer to its training data than the locations to be predicted do, #>   and high when it sits farther. Pass `prediction_points` to compare the #>   two.  # Which of the two suits a map of the sampled square?  Compare each with # the distances from the cells of that map to the training data. cells <- st_make_grid(pts, n = c(20, 20), what = "centers") print(fold_separation(random, pts, sac = 200, prediction_points = cells)) #> Fold separation: random_kfold, 4 fold(s), 200 held-out point(s) (EPSG:32632) #>   autocorrelation range: 200 (in metres, like the distances) #>   prediction target: 400 point(s), measured to each fold's training data #>  #>  fold n_train n_test min_dist median_dist target     gap mean_cor #>     1     150     50    4.696       36.95  37.82 -0.9056     0.57 #>     2     150     50    3.835       42.14  38.02  0.2229     0.55 #>     3     150     50    3.835       38.52  36.00 -1.8310     0.58 #>     4     150     50    4.696       45.79  37.28  3.9360     0.53 #>  #>   Held-out points sit a median of 41.61 from their nearest training #>   point; the closest is 3.835 away. Under the range of 200 that leaves a #>   mean correlation of 0.56 between a held-out point and its nearest #>   training point (exp(-3 d / range) averaged over the hold-out: 1 at #>   distance 0, 0.05 at the range). #>   The prediction points sit a median of 37.48 from the same training data #>   (32.16 from the nearest of all sites). The held-out points sit about as far from their training data as #>   the prediction points do. Matched nearest-neighbour distances do not #>   make a score unbiased by themselves: a learner that draws on several #>   neighbours can still read low on clustered samples. print(fold_separation(blocked, pts, sac = 200, prediction_points = cells)) #> Fold separation: block_kfold, 4 fold(s), 200 held-out point(s) (EPSG:32632) #>   autocorrelation range: 200 (in metres, like the distances) #>   prediction target: 400 point(s), measured to each fold's training data #>  #>  fold n_train n_test n_blocks min_dist median_dist target   gap mean_cor #>     1     152     48        2    23.02       111.9  39.37 58.97     0.23 #>     2     143     57        3    29.04       169.5  44.55 89.14     0.14 #>     3     152     48        2    21.03       118.3  40.95 65.42     0.22 #>     4     153     47        2    21.03       115.9  38.61 67.19     0.23 #>  #>   Held-out points sit a median of 123.5 from their nearest training #>   point; the closest is 21.03 away. Under the range of 200 that leaves a #>   mean correlation of 0.20 between a held-out point and its nearest #>   training point (exp(-3 d / range) averaged over the hold-out: 1 at #>   distance 0, 0.05 at the range). #>   The prediction points sit a median of 40.55 from the same training data #>   (32.16 from the nearest of all sites). Held-out minus prediction: #>   +71.05 in mean distance (W1 71.15); +0.30 on the correlation scale (W1 #>   0.30). The held-out points sit farther from their training data than #>   the prediction points do, so the cross-validated error tends to read #>   high for these prediction points.

title: Forward model selection for geographically weighted regression — gwr_model_selection
code: if (requireNamespace("sp", quietly = TRUE)) {   library(sf)   set.seed(1)   n <- 80   dat <- st_as_sf(     data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000),                a = rnorm(n), b = rnorm(n), noise = rnorm(n)),     coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632   )   dat$z <- 2 * dat$a - dat$b + rnorm(n, 0, 0.5)   sel <- gwr_model_selection(dat, "z", c("a", "b", "noise"), bandwidth = 30)   print(sel)              # every model tried, by AICc, with the gaps   print(sel$best)         # the winning predictor set: a and b, not noise   fit <- fit_gwr_model(dat, "z", sel$best)   fit } #> Geographically weighted regression - forward model selection #>  #>   response    : z #>   candidates  : 3 (a, b, noise) #>   observations: 80 #>   models      : 7 #>   bandwidth   : 30 (adaptive; supplied) #>   kernel      : bisquare #>   criterion   : AICc #>  #>  rank n_vars     variables criterion     delta #>     1      2         a + b  136.6185   0.00000 #>     2      3 a + b + noise  150.6764  14.05793 #>     3      1             a  273.2590 136.64056 #>     4      2     a + noise  278.3346 141.71614 #>     5      1             b  360.8372 224.21866 #>     6      0        <none>  369.4529 232.83444 #>     7      1         noise  378.2502 241.63171 #>  #> Selected: z ~ a + b #>  #> No other model is within 2 of the best; the runner-up is 14.06 away. #>  #> The criterion is in-sample and every model shares one bandwidth. #> Confirm with select_features_forward() before relying on this. #> [1] "a" "b" #> <GWR> spatial model fit #>   Formula : z ~ a + b #>   n       : 80 #>   CRS     : EPSG:32632 #>   Bandwidth: 80 neighbours (adaptive, bisquare kernel) #>   AICc    : 122.82 #>   Eff. parameters: 7.2 of 80 observations

code: library(sf) set.seed(1) n <- 80 site <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000),              elev = rnorm(n)),   coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632 ) site$price <- 10 + 0.01 * (st_coordinates(site)[, 1] - 5e5) +   2 * site$elev + rnorm(n)  # A custom backend: an ordinary linear model behind the spatial_fit interface. lm_fit <- function(train_sf) {   new_spatial_fit(     subclass       = "lm_fit",     engine         = lm(price ~ elev, st_drop_geometry(train_sf)),     formula        = price ~ elev,     response_var   = "price",     predictor_vars = "elev",     data_sf        = train_sf   ) }  # Required: cv_spatial() scores each fold through the predict() generic, # which dispatches on the subclass named above. predict.lm_fit <- function(object, newdata = NULL, ...) {   if (is.null(newdata)) newdata <- object$data_sf   as.numeric(stats::predict(object$engine, st_drop_geometry(newdata))) } registerS3method("predict", "lm_fit", predict.lm_fit)  cv <- cv_spatial(site, "price", "elev", fit_fn = lm_fit, k = 3, seed = 1) #> cv_spatial(): no folds supplied -- using spatial block k-fold CV (k=3). cv$overall #>       RMSE      MAE     MAPE    SMAPE        R2 Adj_R2 n_pred n_MAPE n_SMAPE #> 1 3.472328 3.009688 21.29953 20.27029 0.2341257     NA     80     80      80 # Always check these two agree before trusting the metrics above. c(attempted = cv$n_folds_attempted, succeeded = cv$n_folds_succeeded) #> attempted succeeded  #>         3         3

code: # Any spatial_fit works here; a forest keeps the example free of the # optional GWR/Stan backends. if (requireNamespace("ranger", quietly = TRUE)) {   library(sf)   set.seed(1)   n <- 120   pts <- st_as_sf(     data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000),                elev = rnorm(n)),     coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632   )   pts$price <- 10 + 0.01 * (st_coordinates(pts)[, 1] - 5e5) +     2 * pts$elev + rnorm(n)   fit  <- fit_rf_model(pts, "price", "elev", num_trees = 100, seed = 1)   surf <- predict_surface(fit, n_cells = 500, covariates = pts)   print(surf[".pred"])        # one prediction per grid cell, as an sf layer   # Check where that surface is extrapolating before mapping it. title: Compute Moran's I on the residuals of a fitted spatial model — residual_morans_i
code: # Works on any spatial_fit; a forest keeps the example free of the optional # GWR/Stan backends. if (requireNamespace("ranger", quietly = TRUE)) {   library(sf)   set.seed(1)   n <- 120   dat <- st_as_sf(     data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000),                elev = rnorm(n)),     coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632   )   # A strong east-west trend the predictor cannot explain: the residuals   # should still carry spatial structure, and this is what detects it.   dat$price <- 10 + 0.02 * (st_coordinates(dat)[, 1] - 5e5) +     2 * dat$elev + rnorm(n)   fit <- fit_rf_model(dat, "price", "elev", num_trees = 100, seed = 1)   # I = 0.64, z = 15.5: strong positive residual autocorrelation, exactly   # as constructed.  A z near 0 with a large p-value would be the opposite   # verdict -- no structure the model failed to capture.   residual_morans_i(fit) } #> Residual Moran's I = 0.6437   (E[I] = -0.0084, sd = 0.0419) #>   z = 15.548, p = 1.653e-54 #>   null: randomisation moments, approximate for these residuals; n = 120, df = 119 #>   residual kurtosis 2.371 (3 = Gaussian) #>   weights: 120 x 120 dgCMatrix, 8 neighbour(s) per row; not retained, keep_weights = TRUE to keep it

code: if (requireNamespace("sp", quietly = TRUE)) {   library(sf)   set.seed(1)   n <- 120   pts <- st_as_sf(     data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000),                a = rnorm(n), b = rnorm(n), noise = rnorm(n)),     coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632   )   pts$resp <- 3 * pts$a + 2 * pts$b + rnorm(n, 0, 0.3)    # The learner: a GWR with an adaptive bisquare kernel reaching the 30th   # nearest training point.  With no variables it is the kernel-weighted   # local mean, which is the baseline: a GWR's local intercept beats a   # global mean on any smooth response, so the first variable has to beat   # the local mean under the same kernel.   fit_fn <- function(tr, vars) fit_gwr_model(tr, "resp", vars, bandwidth = 30)   sel <- select_features_forward(pts, "resp", c("a", "b", "noise"), fit_fn,                                  k = 3, quiet = TRUE)   sel$selected   sel$baseline$type        # "null model": step 1 was tested against it   sel$history[sel$history$step <= 1, c("step", "variable", "score", "gain")]    # A learner that cannot fit an empty set takes its no-predictor model   # through `null_fn`.  Here the same local mean, written as a spatial_fit   # of its own with a predict() method, for a learner that insists on a   # variable.  Without `null_fn` that sweep would start from the mean of   # each training fold.   needs_one <- function(tr, vars) {     if (!length(vars)) stop("this learner needs a predictor")     fit_gwr_model(tr, "resp", vars, bandwidth = 30)   }   local_mean <- function(tr, bandwidth = 30) {     new_spatial_fit("local_mean_fit",                     engine = list(xy = st_coordinates(tr), y = tr$resp,                                   bandwidth = bandwidth),                     formula = resp ~ 1, response_var = "resp",                     predictor_vars = character(0), data_sf = tr)   }   predict.local_mean_fit <- function(object, newdata = NULL, ...) {     e  <- object$engine     at <- if (is.null(newdata)) e$xy else st_coordinates(newdata)     vapply(seq_len(nrow(at)), function(i) {       d <- sqrt((e$xy[, 1] - at[i, 1])^2 + (e$xy[, 2] - at[i, 2])^2)       h <- sort(d)[min(e$bandwidth, length(d))]  # the kernel's reach here       w <- ifelse(d > h, 0, (1 - d^2 / h^2)^2)   # bisquare weights       sum(w * e$y) / sum(w)     }, numeric(1))   }   registerS3method("predict", "local_mean_fit", predict.local_mean_fit)   sel2 <- select_features_forward(pts, "resp", c("a", "b", "noise"), needs_one,                                   k = 3, quiet = TRUE, null_fn = local_mean)   sel2$baseline$type       # "null_fn"   all.equal(sel2$baseline$score, sel$baseline$score)  # the same baseline } #> [1] TRUE

The # correction is large here, and meant to be: about 22 points per cell that # all share the cell's part of the trend carry far fewer than 22 # independent pieces of information about the cell mean. naive <- summarize_by_cell(assigned, response_var = "val", estimate = "mean") kish  <- summarize_by_cell(assigned, response_var = "val", deff = "kish",                            estimate = "mean") data.frame(n = naive$n,            se_naive = naive$..se_resp_val,            se_kish  = kish$..se_resp_val) #>    n   se_naive   se_kish #> 1 25 0.09706775 0.7210227 #> 2 28 0.11815220 0.9279034 #> 3 25 0.11573069 0.8596517 #> 4 21 0.11556510 0.7881134 #> 5 23 0.13192931 0.9407000 #> 6 21 0.12707224 0.8665880 #> 7 10 0.18215988 0.8673238 #> 8 27 0.09534639 0.7355266 #> 9 20 0.14402822 0.9590654 attr(kish, "deff_applied")   # code: if (requireNamespace("gstat", quietly = TRUE)) {   library(sf)   # An exponential field with range parameter 200 (true effective range   # 600 m) on a 1 km square, with a nugget of 0.6 on a unit sill.   set.seed(4)   n <- 400   xy <- data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000))   D  <- as.matrix(dist(xy))   xy$z <- as.numeric(t(chol(exp(-D / 200) + diag(0.6, n))) %*% rnorm(n))   pts <- st_as_sf(xy, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632)   prof <- resolution_profile(pts, response_var = "z", n_levels = 12)    # print() is explicit because only the last value of a braced block is   # shown, and the table is the thing worth seeing here.   print(summary(prof))   print(attr(summary(prof), "common")) # the levels all of them accept, if any   attr(summary(prof), "bands")         # each criterion's region in full } #> Resolution picks: 3 criteria over 12 levels (2 to 44 cells) #>  #>   cells: density-weighted k-means++ starts (power 1, 8 neighbours) #>  #>    criterion best flat region levels in band #>           cp   44          44              1 #>  reliability    4      4 to 6              3 #>          loo   44          44              1 #>  #>   cp, loo: the optimum is the support ceiling (n / min_cell_n). #>   reliability: the optimum is the range floor (area / range^2). #>   There the bound is choosing, not the criterion. #>  #>   picks span 4 to 44 cells (11.0x) #>   no level is in every flat region: the criteria disagree over the #>   whole ladder. plot() draws the curves they were read from. #> integer(0) #> $cp #> [1] 44 #>  #> $reliability #> [1] 4 5 6 #>  #> $loo #> [1] 44 #>

title: spatialkit 2.0.0
text: New fit_rf_model() cv_rf(): ranger random forest first-class backend, returning rf_fit works cv_spatial(), predict_surface(), area_of_applicability() plot() like model. Three defaults opinionated: include_coords = FALSE (forest given coordinates memorises location fails wherever — Meyer et al. 2019, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecolmodel.2019.108815 — random CV catch ); fitted() returns --bag predictions, summary() rf_fit comparable backends says ($info$fitted_are_oob); importance defaults permutation rather impurity, biased toward continuous high-cardinality predictors (Strobl et al. 2007, https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2105-8-25). Compare backends compare_models_cv(), now RF branch. predict() rf_fit refuses type confusions ranger otherwise absorb silently: numeric--fit predictor supplied text (ranger factor-codes, applies numeric split thresholds codes), logical--fit predictor supplied text, categorical level forest never grown — level set enough, since spatial fold holding whole class leaves level training rows. Arguments make ranger return matrix (predict.= TRUE, type = "quantiles") rejected rather flattened column-major. constant seed supplied ranger’s predict unless caller passes one, prediction consume global RNG predict_surface(chunk_size = ) — performance knob — shift later random draws. cv_rf(seed = ) reaches forest every fold, gains pointize. Passing ranger’s spelling argument wrapper already sets (num.trees, min.node.size, num.threads, mtry, importance, seed) ... error naming wrapper argument use, rather reaching ranger() twice. num_threads defaults getOption("mc.cores", 1L) — one thread unless session opted — fit predict(), rather ranger’s default every core machine, cv_rf(parallel = ) runs forked fold’s forest one thread unless told otherwise, worker count never multiplied thread count. See ?fit_rf_model. Every cv_*() compare_models_cv() accept folds vector fold labels, one per row — make_folds()$assignment$fold, object naturally hand — addition make_folds() result list train/test splits, three shapes area_of_applicability() already took. label vector used fail R’s “$ operator invalid atomic vectors”. New area_of_applicability(), implementing dissimilarity index Meyer & Pebesma (2021, https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.13650). Predictors centred scaled training data’s statistics, optionally weighted variable importance — importance , square root, matching CAST. prediction point’s DI distance nearest training point space mean pairwise training distance, threshold outlier-removed maximum training data’s DI. Pass make_folds() result actually validated — area defined relative performance estimate, blocked estimate claim predicting away. model fitted include_coords = TRUE measured coordinate space, since index ignores location report point far outside training extent inside ordinary covariate values alone; weights two coordinate columns default mean supplied, caller never seen . Non-POINT newdata reduced points, CRS present one side applied . zero-variance test relative column’s magnitude rather absolute tolerance, predictor dropped unit recorded . Categorical predictors refused rather dummy-coded; logicals read 0/1. make_folds() result resolved ..row_id values, coincide row positions input carried prior IDs. See ?area_of_applicability. New select_features_forward(): greedy forward feature selection spatially blocked inner folds, whole point . Random inner folds inside blocked outer folds select variables look predictive nearby points leak train test, outer loop reports honest-looking numbers dishonestly chosen feature set. method defaults "block_kfold" logs warning set "random_kfold". empty set scored first backend can fit , first variable judged null-model baseline rather accepted unconditionally, history carries baseline step = 0 row. Every candidate set scored observations — completeness filter matches prep_model_data() exactly, finiteness test included, candidate carrying single Inf preferred easier subset — inner folds built , sweep, rather rebuilt per candidate. max_fits budget guards nesting sweep inside leave-one-outer folds. backend fit empty set — fit_rf_model() fit_gwr_model() refuse zero-length predictor_vars — probe silent console: per-fold failures go file trace , rather printing lines genuinely failed run prints. New gwr_model_selection(): wraps GWmodel::gwr.model.selection() (Lu et al. 2014, https://doi.org/10.1080/10095020.2014.917453) returns ranked table instead two loosely-coupled lists. fast, -sample counterpart select_features_forward() — forward search scored AICc, read documented c(bandwidth, AIC, AICc, RSS) layout GWmodel’s GWR.df, carries column names; result records whether table arrived shape. Candidates must numeric, dmat_max_n = Inf means always precompute distance matrix. limitations documented rather papered : one bandwidth shared every candidate (makes criteria comparable), null model never evaluated, result always names least one predictor. disagrees blocked estimate, believe blocked estimate. See ?gwr_model_selection. New predict_surface(): builds regular grid training extent (grid supply), joins covariates, predicts chunks returns sf. Supports boundary clipping, cell_size approximate n_cells, se = TRUE posterior-SD surface backend exposes draws. New plot() method spatial_fit, type = "residuals", "observed_predicted" "variogram" (empirical residual variogram fitted model effective range overlaid, fit can judged rather trusted). variogram’s distance axis labelled units CRS actually fitted — metres auto-chosen zone lon/lat fit, caller’s degrees — names azimuth single direction drawn, fit converge says caption.
